title: APE SCALES: hang the coconuts, then the ape jumps. Perfect balance, or everything crashes (free, browser)
author: office-canard
selftext:
APE SCALES is a free balance puzzle you can play in the browser.



Play: [https://office-canard.itch.io/ape-scales](https://office-canard.itch.io/ape-scales)



A hanging scale branches into hooks. You hang numbered coconuts on the hooks, and last of all the ape jumps on. That jump is your final answer. You're sure it works, you worry something is off, and you jump anyway. Perfect balance, or everything comes crashing down. 100 stages, each with exactly one answer.



Honestly, I don't like math. Once the numbers get hard, I start to hate my own puzzle. But I'm certain there are people all over the world who love exactly this. That's why I made it.



How AI fit in



\- Code: Claude wrote it.

\- Stages: Claude built a counter that checks every stage has exactly one answer, counting ape placement, total-weight multiples and how the coconuts are split. Then it made a difficulty index and ordered about 930,000 candidates into 100 stages, using 22 stages I picked as difficulty landmarks. Since I'm not a math person, the spec keeps "a person can solve it" marked as unverified, separate from what a machine can check.

\- Testing: on every change, Claude auto-solved all 100 stages in a browser before pushing.

\- Art: the ape is pixel art I made with Gemini. A code-built ape and a free 3D model both looked wrong. Claude handled the integration and motion. The scale and ropes are drawn in code.

\- Sound: all sound effects are synthesized. For music, I swapped the steel drum for kalimba samples because it sounded better on phone speakers. Claude can't hear audio, so I judged every track by ear.

\- One rule we kept: early on, Claude had quietly added a rule that the ape could only hang from an empty hook. I caught it. Since then: the AI never adds rules without saying so.



Feedback welcome, especially from people who love number puzzles more than I do.
